audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's tracked ability was 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' — an ability Hwei does not have. It appeared in focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and reports 1, 3, 5 and 9. Separately, wants.foe[2] and spikes[1].text called Spiraling Despair a fear, and spikes[3].text and the late paragraph called it an execute.
audit.why: Hwei's E is Subject: Torment, the crowd-control palette (Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw) on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10. The fear is Grim Visage inside that palette. Spiraling Despair is his R: 120/100/80, 1300 range, an expanding painting centred on the first champion hit that slows and explodes at maximum size or on the target's death — not a fear and not an execute.
audit.corrected: Every instance replaced with Subject: Torment (E) and Grim Visage, and the ultimate described as the expanding zone it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content chart gave Brand six of seven — which the packet flags directly against a 46.98% win rate over 464 games.
audit.why: Brand's level 3 E-Q package wins a short trade, so the first three rows are genuinely his. From 4-5 the palettes out-range him, and from level 6 Spiraling Despair opens fights from 1300 range while Subject: Serenity shields the burst he answers with. A sub-50% record is that shape.
audit.corrected: Brand, Brand, Brand, Skill, Hwei, Hwei, Hwei — proposed as one group with the matching win[] rows and rewritten whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text placed Hwei's turning point 'late', with level 6 described as still Brand's.
audit.why: Spiraling Despair at 6 is a 1300-range opener against a champion whose longest spell is 1050 and who owns no dash. That is the spike, not a late-game ceiling.
audit.corrected: Level 6 onward reassigned in both charts and stated in the phases whys and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit, and the packet flags no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: The palette cooldowns are the whole sequencing problem: Subject: Torment 12s, Subject: Serenity 18s, Spiraling Despair 120s.
audit.corrected: All three written in, phrased as when to step up.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim.
audit.why: Bullet bodies must match their own titles.
audit.corrected: Replaced; the don't now carries the Subject: Serenity shield, which was absent from the page entirely.

audit.whatIsWrong: Brand's W carries a derived 'terrain' flag.
audit.why: Riot's Pillar of Flame text is delayed area damage only; it creates no terrain.

edits.before: This is the one phase where Hwei can flip the script — his full rotation (fear lockdown into E slow into R execute) threatens real burst damage if he lands it clean on an isolated target, and a well-piloted Hwei with items can out-trade you in a single well-executed combo. Play carefully around vision and positioning in late-game skirmishes, since this is where his kit's ceiling can outpace your own.
edits.after: This is where Hwei takes over — Grim Visage's fear off the Subject: Torment palette into a chained paint rotation, with Spiraling Despair expanding around you from 1300 range, threatens real damage on an isolated target. It is not an execute; it is a growing zone you have to walk out of, so move the moment it attaches. Play around vision, never be the closest body to his side of a fight, and hold Zhonya's for the painting rather than for the chip.
